Houston Weather: Rain returns for Friday and Halloween, stormy cold front blows in on Election Day - ABC13 Houston 
 24/7 Live Houston Southwest Southeast Northwest Northeast Need to Know Weather 
 Rain returns for Friday and Halloween, stormy cold front blows in on Election Day 
 By Travis Herzog , David Tillman , Elita Loresca , Kevin Roth , Elyse Smith Friday, October 30, 2026 11:18PM 
 An active jet stream pattern will bring rain chances through Election Day when a stormy cold front pushes through the state. HOUSTON, Texas (KTRK) -- An active Pacific jet stream now tracking through Texas is pushing rain into the area this afternoon and evening. Next week, a more powerful system will approach on Election Day to bring a stormy cold front into Houston.
 We have the rain chance at 60% today, so prepare for the possibility of some wet Friday night football games!
 What's the weather outlook for Halloween?
 We should prepare for a very warm, humid day with a 40% chance of showers and thunderstorms, especially in the afternoon. Lows will be around 70 with a high in the mid 80s. Temperatures will fall back toward 80 at the start of trick-or-treat time with high humidity. Some of that rain could linger past 5PM, but overall we expect the rain to diminish as the evening wears on. Just prepare for sticky air that could leave you sweating under that costume.
 And what about for Election Day?
 A big dip in the jet stream will likely send a strong storm system into the Plains on Election Day, which will force a stormy cold front into Texas as voters head to the polls. This is the kind of weather pattern that could bring strong storms with heavy rain and gusty winds. It's a bit too early to nail down the exact timing, storm strength, and impacts here around Houston, so stay tuned! For now, we expect the bulk of the rain in the afternoon and evening. If you don't want to risk dealing with bad weather on Election Day, you might consider taking advantage of early voting, which runs through 7 p.m. Friday.
 What are you tracking in the tropics?
 We are monitoring what's left of Pacific storm Vance as moisture spreads into Mexico and Texas. For a more in-depth discussion on what's happening in the tropics, visit our Daily Tropical Update page .
